scenario.title: MANCHURIAN OFFENSIVE - 9 AUG 1945
intro.text:
MANCHURIAN OFFENSIVE - 9 AUG 1945

Khabarovsk, Far Eastern Russia

At the Tehran and Yalta Conference, the Soviet Union has promised to enter the Pacific Theater within three months after the end of the war in Europe. So we are going to smash the Japanese puppet state of Manchukuo with a powerful operation. Your task is to overcome the border rivers near Khabarovsk and quickly advance westward into the interior!

ORDERS
Capture all VH!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-briliant.text: The roads east of Vienna were closed before the retreat formed another belt. Ten days later the city fell, and Europe finally stopped supplying new place names for our maps.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-victory.text: The pursuit reached Vienna with enough guns to finish the battle. The city fell on 13 April; the orders sending us east arrived before the rubble cooled.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-tactical.text: Vienna fell after a hard pursuit and a harder urban battle. We reached the end of Europe with a force already being measured for another railway journey.
line.reaction-lose.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.reaction-lose.text: The pursuit failed to prevent a new defence before Vienna. Other armies finished the city battle; this group crossed the continent carrying the knowledge that Europe did not end with its victory.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.callback-choice-a.text: Before Vienna you closed the western exits but ordered lanes left for civilians. Officers who thought restraint would slow the pursuit now cite your traffic plan as if it were theirs.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: You secured the roads toward Vienna junction by junction. The guns arrived, the city fell ten days later, and Antonov has spent those ten days calculating how much farther the first tanks might have gone.
line.scene-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-0.text: European place names have been erased from the board and replaced by rivers, railways, and distances most of the staff last studied before 1941. Veteran formations recognise the procedure; none recognises the country ahead.
line.scene-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.scene-1.text: The tanks came from Europe by rail, followed by workshops, pontoons, and men who thought Prague was the last station of their war. Now the bridges must carry all of it across rivers absent from their old maps.
line.scene-2.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.scene-2.text: Volkov has put the Seseña report beside the river map. The paper is yellow, the argument is not. Even Antonov has stopped pretending he remembers only the tanks.
line.decision.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.decision.text: We can force the crossings on the first timetable and pursue before the defence understands the scale of the attack, or build secure bridgeheads that can carry the whole army into the interior.
line.decision.choice.race-beyond-the-riv: Force the crossings at once and send mobile columns west before resistance can organise.
Release a nine-strength T-34/85 detachment with 70 experience and fully refuel the core; priority rail movement costs 120 prestige.
line.decision.choice.build-the-bridgehea: Secure every crossing with engineers, artillery, and supply before releasing the pursuit.
Attach a full-strength 1943 engineer detachment with 70 experience, fully replenish ammunition, and give artillery 15 experience; bridging trains cost 100 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-a-0.text: The first columns carry fuel and bridging stores ahead of everything else. Once across, they do not wait for a European-style front to form around them.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-a-1.text: This is the wager I wanted in Spain. Now I want fuel reports, bridge classes, and a turning hour with it. Nine years have made speed more demanding, not less.
line.choice-a-2.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-2.text: The first column crosses on schedule. Miss two reports and the following guns halt at the river, however far the tanks claim to see.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-b-0.text: The bridgeheads are the operation's foundation. The pursuit begins when roads, guns, and ambulances can cross the same river as the tanks.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-b-1.text: Nine years ago I would have called the bridgehead a delay. Build it. When the guns and ambulances are across, give me the road before Volkov finds another river.
line.post-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.post-0.text: From Madrid to Khabarovsk, the recurring question has never been speed or strength alone. It has been whether command can turn either one into an operation that survives its first success.
epilogue.manchuria-tempo-success.speaker: Anna Sokolova
epilogue.manchuria-tempo-success.text: The river line broke before the Kwantung Army could make a front of it. When Japan capitulated, our leading columns were still moving west. You chose the wager Antonov first offered in Spain—and this time the roads, radios, bridges, and guns all kept pace with the tanks.
epilogue.manchuria-bridgehead-success.te: The bridgeheads carried guns, fuel, and ambulances before they carried the pursuit. When Japan capitulated, every column beyond the rivers still belonged to the same operation. Volkov will say he taught you that. I will say it took him nine years to make caution move this fast.
epilogue.manchuria-tempo-defeat.speaker: Sergei Volkov
epilogue.manchuria-tempo-defeat.text: The leading columns crossed, ran beyond their guns, and stopped as separate detachments. Japan's capitulation ended the wider war, but not our accounting. After nine years, the first lesson returned unchanged: distance gained is not yet an operation.
epilogue.manchuria-bridgehead-defeat.tex: The crossings were orderly and the force remained intact, but the border defence did not break before the war ended. We preserved the instrument and failed to make it decisive. Caution can prevent a defeat; it cannot, by itself, produce a victory.
